proposal.summary: A heap buffer overflow in the HFS+ partition file parser of ClamAV (certain versions) due to missing buffer size check may allow unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or crash the scanning process.
proposal.affected_product: ClamAV versions 1.0.0 and earlier, 0.105.1 and earlier, and 0.103.7 and earlier

AV.quote: An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted HFS+ partition file to be scanned by ClamAV on an affected device.

AC.quote: This vulnerability is due to a missing buffer size check that may result in a heap buffer overflow write.

PR.quote: An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted HFS+ partition file to be scanned by ClamAV on an affected device.

UI.quote: An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted HFS+ partition file to be scanned by ClamAV on an affected device.

S.quote: A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the ClamAV scanning process, or else crash the process, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Obtain the ClamAV advisory or vendor patch information linked in the report and determine fixed versions and available mitigations; coordinate disclosure and prepare updates for affected deployments.

evidence_quotes.quote: A vulnerability in the HFS+ partition file parser of ClamAV versions 1.0.0 and earlier, 0.105.1 and earlier, and 0.103.7 and earlier could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary code.
This vulnerability is due to a missing buffer size check that may result in a heap buffer overflow write.
An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted HFS+ partition file to be scanned by ClamAV on an affected device.

A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the ClamAV scanning process, or else crash the process, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition.
For a description of this vulnerability, see the ClamAV blog ["https://blog.clamav.net/"].
